strengths: Large-scale, multi-faceted dataset curation: The paper curates and synthesizes Vlaser-6M, covering grounding, spatial reasoning, robotic QA, planning, and in-domain robot simulation data across multiple embodiments.

Extensive and rigorous upstream evaluation: The model is evaluated across 12 diverse embodied reasoning benchmarks at both 2B and 8B scales, showing solid improvements over the base InternVL3 and competitive/superior performance relative to recent open and proprietary baselines.

Insightful negative finding on VLM-to-VLA transfer: The authors honestly report and analyze that upstream gains on standard Internet/egocentric embodied reasoning benchmarks do not readily translate to downstream closed-loop control, highlighting that in-domain robotic viewpoint alignment is far more consequential.

Execution of closed-loop evaluations: Incorporating SimplerEnv evaluations on standard WidowX and Google Robot tasks provides concrete closed-loop control verification rather than relying solely on open-loop metrics.
weaknesses: Conceptual tension with the paper's title/premise: The title highlights 'Synergistic Embodied Reasoning', yet the empirical findings in Tables 2 and 3 demonstrate that generic embodied reasoning pretraining (Vlaser-2B) provides negligible downstream VLA benefits over the raw InternVL3-2B baseline (e.g., 43.2% vs 41.8% on WidowX; 51.3% vs 54.7% on Google Robot variant aggregation). The primary improvements stem from adding in-domain robot QA/grounding data, which indicates domain alignment rather than general synergy.

Limited architectural novelty: The architecture couples an off-the-shelf InternVL3 backbone with a standard flow-matching action expert following π0/prior VLA designs. The core technical novelty lies predominantly in dataset curation and empirical analysis.

Lack of 8B VLA evaluation and real-world robot experiments: Closed-loop policy fine-tuning is only demonstrated for the 2B model, leaving open the question of whether an 8B backbone could better leverage upstream embodied reasoning. Additionally, all policy evaluations are confined to SimplerEnv without physical robot verification.
Presentation flaws: The abstract ends abruptly with an unfinished sentence ('The code, model and data are available at').

strengths: Comprehensive empirical benchmarking across 12 diverse embodied reasoning datasets spanning QA, planning, visual grounding, and spatial intelligence.

Valuable and honest empirical insight: the authors systematically show that general out-of-domain embodied reasoning pretraining yields negligible gains on downstream closed-loop manipulation, whereas in-domain QA/grounding data directly reduces observation domain shift and boosts performance.
Large-scale curated dataset (Vlaser-6M) integrating automated generation pipelines across spatial 3D data, SA-1B grounding, and simulation environments, with open-source commitments.
weaknesses: Mismatch between paper framing and empirical findings: The title and abstract emphasize 'synergistic embodied reasoning' bridging VLM reasoning with VLA control, yet the paper's core experimental result shows that general embodied reasoning pretraining does not cleanly transfer to closed-loop VLA control.

Limited architectural novelty: The model design directly follows established paradigms, combining an off-the-shelf VLM backbone (InternVL3) with a flow-matching action expert head as pioneered by π0 and related works.

Absence of real-world robot experiments: Closed-loop control evaluations are conducted exclusively in SimplerEnv. While SimplerEnv is a reputable simulation suite, validating the transfer of in-domain reasoning to physical robot hardware is critical for embodied AI.

Omission of downstream VLA evaluations for the 8B model: Although Vlaser-8B demonstrates the strongest upstream reasoning scores in Table 1, downstream VLA policy experiments in Tables 2 and 3 are only reported for the 2B model scale.

Potential benchmark contamination and training distribution overlap: Several training subsets closely mirror benchmark tasks and source datasets (e.g., ScanNet/VSI-Bench templates, SA-1B), but the paper lacks discussion or ablations regarding decontamination or zero-shot generalization vs. memorization.

strengths: Large-scale empirical curation effort: The authors assemble a large-scale multimodal dataset (Vlaser-6M) spanning visual grounding, spatial reasoning, task planning, and simulation-based QA.

Comprehensive benchmark evaluation for VLM reasoning: The model is evaluated across 12 different embodied reasoning benchmarks, achieving competitive or superior numbers compared to open-source baselines and proprietary models on several metrics.

Honest empirical finding on transferability: The paper identifies a significant and candid finding regarding VLM-to-VLA transfer—specifically that broad, out-of-domain embodied reasoning pre-training provides minimal benefit (or even slight regressions) to downstream closed-loop manipulation, highlighting the crucial role of in-domain robotic data.
weaknesses: Disconnection between central claims and empirical findings: The title and introduction advertise a 'Synergistic Embodied Reasoning' foundation model bridging high-level reasoning and low-level control. However, the experimental findings in Section 3.2 demonstrate the opposite: generic embodied reasoning pretraining (Vlaser-2B) barely improves upon the baseline InternVL3-2B on WidowX (43.2% vs. 41.8%) and actually degrades performance on Google Robot Variant Aggregation (51.3% vs. 54.7%). Meaningful gains only emerge when adding synthetic in-domain QA pairs directly sampled from the target robot environments, contradicting the premise that general embodied reasoning enhances policy execution.

Limited architectural and methodological novelty: The method combines an existing VLM backbone (InternVL3) with a standard flow-matching action expert (directly following architectures established in prior work such as pi0). The data engine largely aggregates previously published datasets (RoboPoint, SA-1B, ScanNet, EgoPlan) augmented with synthetic question-answer generation via Qwen2.5-VL, offering modest methodological advancement.

Evaluation limited to simulation without physical robot validation: Downstream control is evaluated exclusively within SimplerEnv simulation benchmarks. While SimplerEnv correlates with real-world outcomes, demonstrating closed-loop transfer on physical hardware is standard and critical for claiming a foundational VLA model.

Risk of benchmark contamination in upstream reasoning: Many benchmarks evaluated in Table 1 (such as Paco-Lavis, Pixmo-Points, Where2place, Pointarena, VSI-Bench, RefSpatial) share direct sources or closely overlapping data distributions with the training splits used in Vlaser-6M, making it difficult to disentangle genuine generalization from distribution-specific memorization.

Drafting and proofreading oversights: The manuscript contains notable careless errors, such as Figure 1 caption referring to a radar/spider chart as 'A LiDAR visualization' (presumably an uncorrected mistranslation), and the abstract ending abruptly with 'The code, model and data are available at' without providing a URL or placeholder.

strengths: Comprehensive upstream evaluation across 12 distinct embodied reasoning benchmarks (covering spatial reasoning, visual grounding, planning, and embodied QA), demonstrating consistent improvements over strong baselines such as Qwen2.5-VL, RoboBrain2.0, and Embodied-R1.

Provides an important and actionable empirical finding for the VLA community: general out-of-domain embodied reasoning pre-training yields negligible improvements on downstream closed-loop control, whereas in-domain multimodal reasoning data substantially enhances downstream manipulation success.
Evaluation across multiple robotic manipulation environments and embodiments in simulation (WidowX and Google Robot in SimplerEnv, Aloha-AgileX in RoboTwin).
Detailed documentation of the data generation and filtering pipeline (Vlaser-6M) using an LLM-as-a-judge verification mechanism validated with human agreement analysis.
weaknesses: No physical robot experiments: All downstream closed-loop evaluations are strictly conducted within simulated environments (SimplerEnv and RoboTwin). While SimplerEnv has demonstrated real-to-sim correlation, hardware deployment is missing to validate real-world dynamics, lighting shifts, and sensor noise.
Limited architectural novelty: The modeling framework largely combines existing components—InternVL3 as the VLM backbone and a flow-matching action expert module following recent paradigms like π0.

Omission of downstream VLA results for the 8B model: The downstream manipulation evaluations (Tables 2, 3, 4, and 5) only evaluate Vlaser-2B variants. It remains unclear whether the findings hold and how much performance scales when using the Vlaser-8B backbone for action control.

The in-domain data advantage may primarily reflect visual domain adaptation rather than reasoning transfer: Because the 2M in-domain samples are derived directly from the evaluation environments/embodiments, the observed gains could be largely attributed to mitigating visual distribution shifts rather than synergistic reasoning transfer.

strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation across 12 diverse embodied reasoning benchmarks spanning visual question answering, spatial reasoning, grounding, and high-level planning.
Substantial data curation effort resulting in the Vlaser-6M dataset, supported by well-documented data filtering protocols and LLM-as-a-judge quality assurance.

A valuable negative finding regarding transferability: standard out-of-domain embodied reasoning pretraining contributes marginally to low-level closed-loop robot control, highlighting the visual and perspective gap between web-scale datasets and robotic manipulation setups.
Consistent performance improvements demonstrated across multiple simulated benchmarks (SimplerEnv with WidowX and Google Robot, and RoboTwin with Aloha).
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: the framework essentially pairs an off-the-shelf vision-language model (InternVL3) with a flow-matching action expert following the design of recent models like pi_0.

Potential domain-overfitting / circularity in the in-domain VLA experiments: the 2M in-domain multimodal pretraining data is synthesized directly from the simulation platforms (SimplerEnv and RoboTwin) used for downstream evaluation. It is unsurprising that visual representations pre-aligned to these specific camera viewpoints and scene distributions improve downstream policy learning, leaving broader generalization to unobserved real-world scenes questionable.
Absence of real-world robotic validation: despite the paper focusing on vision-language-action control, experiments are exclusively confined to simulation environments.

Missing 8B model evaluation in downstream VLA control: while both 2B and 8B scales are evaluated on upstream reasoning benchmarks in Table 1, all downstream control experiments (Tables 2, 3, 4, and 5) evaluate only the 2B model, leaving the scaling behavior of the full VLA pipeline unexplored.

Lack of statistical significance reporting: downstream success rates in Tables 2, 3, and 4 are reported as single-point metrics across tasks without confidence intervals or multi-seed variance, which is critical for noisy robotic evaluation rollouts.

strengths: Important and timely empirical insight: The paper investigates a critical yet under-explored question in embodied AI—whether improvements on upstream vision-language embodied reasoning benchmarks translate to downstream low-level robot control (VLA). The finding that out-of-domain embodied reasoning data fails to improve downstream control, whereas in-domain multimodal data significantly boosts VLA fine-tuning, provides valuable guidance for data curation in the robotics community.

Extensive and comprehensive evaluation: The model is evaluated across 12 diverse upstream embodied reasoning benchmarks (covering QA, planning, grounding, and spatial intelligence) against both proprietary (GPT-4o, Claude-3.7, Gemini-2.5) and open-source models, as well as downstream closed-loop manipulation across three robot setups (WidowX and Google Robot in SimplerEnv, Aloha-AgileX in RoboTwin).

Substantial data engineering effort (Vlaser-6M): The authors construct a rich 6M dataset spanning grounding, 3D spatial perception, planning, and in-domain simulation QA, complemented by a rigorous LLM-as-a-judge filtering pipeline validated against human evaluations.

Strong empirical performance: Vlaser-8B achieves state-of-the-art results across most upstream reasoning benchmarks among open-source models of comparable scale, and downstream fine-tuning outperforms competitive baselines like OpenVLA, SpatialVLA, and π0.
weaknesses: Lack of physical robot experiments: All downstream closed-loop manipulation evaluations are performed entirely in simulation (SimplerEnv and RoboTwin). Although SimplerEnv offers validated real-to-sim correlation, physical robot verification under real-world sensing and physics noise would significantly reinforce the conclusions.

Incremental architectural novelty: The architecture primarily combines an existing VLM backbone (InternVL3) with a flow-matching action expert (resembling π0 and related action chunking architectures). The core value lies in the data engine and empirical analysis rather than new modeling paradigms.

Conflation of domain adaptation with embodied reasoning: The paper attributes the downstream improvements of in-domain data to reasoning QA, but does not clearly disentangle the effect of visual in-domain feature adaptation (i.e., simply exposing the vision encoder to the target environment's visual distribution via autoencoding or basic captioning) from the specific benefits of high-level embodied reasoning structures.

Minor presentation issues: Incomplete links/placeholders in the abstract ('The code, model and data are available at'), and the explanation of the normalized average metric in Table 1 lacks explicit normalization details.
